entries.title: Bad block on disk
entries.what: The disk reported a sector it could not read. Data in that area may be lost and the disk may be failing.
causes: Bad SATA/USB cable or enclosure (external disks)
fix: Back up important data now
Check SMART health (CrystalDiskInfo, or: Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter)
Run chkdsk /r on the volume
Replace the disk if errors repeat

entries.title: Disk controller error
entries.what: The driver detected a controller error on the disk.
fix: Reseat/replace the cable; try another port
Check SMART health
Update storage controller drivers and BIOS

entries.title: Disk not ready
entries.summary: Device {0} is not ready for access
entries.what: A disk was not ready when Windows tried to access it.
causes: Disk spinning up or going to sleep
fix: Harmless once for removable drives; if repeated on internal disks check power settings and disk health

entries.title: Error during paging operation
entries.what: An error occurred while Windows read or wrote the page file or memory-mapped data on this disk.
fix: Check SMART health and cables
If it is a USB drive, check whether it was unplugged at that time

entries.title: Disk predicts it will fail (SMART)
entries.summary: SMART warning: {0} predicts it will fail
entries.what: The disk's own self-monitoring (SMART) reported that it is likely to fail soon.
fix: Back up immediately
Replace the disk

entries.title: Disk I/O was retried
entries.what: A read/write to the disk did not complete in time and had to be retried. Occasional retries are tolerable; many are an early sign of trouble.
causes: Outdated storage driver or SSD firmware
Aggressive power saving on the disk/controller
fix: Check SMART health
Update SSD firmware and the storage controller driver
Replace the SATA cable
Disable link power management for the disk if it happens after idle

entries.title: Disk was surprise-removed
entries.what: A disk disappeared without being safely removed.
fix: Harmless for USB drives removed on purpose; otherwise check cables and power

entries.title: Storage controller reset a device
entries.what: The SATA (AHCI) driver reset a disk because it stopped responding.
causes: SSD firmware or power management issue
fix: Check SMART health
Replace the SATA cable
Update SSD firmware and chipset drivers

entries.title: NVMe controller reset
entries.what: The NVMe driver reset an SSD because it stopped responding.
fix: Update SSD firmware
Check SSD temperature
Try disabling PCIe Link State Power Management in the power plan

entries.title: NVMe controller error
entries.what: The NVMe driver reported a controller error.
fix: Update SSD firmware
Check SMART health
Reseat the SSD

entries.title: Intel RST reset a device
entries.what: The Intel Rapid Storage driver reset a disk that stopped responding.
fix: Update Intel RST driver
Check disk health and cable

entries.title: File system corruption detected
entries.what: NTFS found a corrupted structure on a volume.
fix: Run chkdsk /f on the volume (needs restart for C:)
Check disk health
If it repeats, test RAM

entries.title: File system corruption detected
entries.what: NTFS found a corrupted structure on a volume.
fix: Run chkdsk /f on the volume (needs restart for C:)
Check disk health

entries.title: Volume health check
entries.what: Windows checked a volume when it was mounted. The message says whether it is healthy or needs repair.
fix: If the message says the volume needs to be repaired, run chkdsk /f

entries.title: File system structure repaired
entries.what: NTFS self-healing repaired a corrupted file system structure.
causes: Earlier corruption (crash, power loss, failing disk)
fix: Harmless if rare; if repeated, check disk health

entries.title: Failed to flush data to the transaction log
entries.what: Windows could not write data to the disk's transaction log. Corruption may occur.
causes: Disk removed or disconnected while in use
fix: If it is a USB drive, always use Safely Remove
Check disk health and cables

entries.title: Transaction resource manager failed to start
entries.what: The NTFS transaction (TxF) metadata on a volume is corrupted.
fix: Usually fixed by: fsutil resource setautoreset true C:\ and a restart

entries.title: Crash dump initialization failed
entries.what: Windows could not prepare to save a memory dump if it crashes, so a future blue screen may leave no dump.
causes: No or too small page file on the system drive
fix: Make sure C: has a system-managed page file
Check System > Advanced > Startup and Recovery settings

entries.title: Page file for crash dump could not be configured
entries.what: The page file is too small or missing, so crash dumps cannot be written.
causes: Page file disabled or too small
fix: Set the page file to System managed on C:

entries.title: Crash dump could not be created
entries.what: A blue screen happened but the memory dump could not be written.
fix: Set the page file to System managed
Check disk health

entries.title: Shadow copies deleted (no space to grow)
entries.what: Shadow copies (restore points / backup snapshots) were deleted because their storage area could not grow.
causes: Very heavy disk writes during backup
fix: Free disk space
Increase shadow storage: vssadmin resize shadowstorage

entries.title: Oldest shadow copy deleted to stay within limit
entries.what: The oldest shadow copy was removed to keep shadow storage under its size limit. Normal rotation.

entries.title: Shadow copies aborted (storage could not grow)
entries.what: Shadow copies were aborted because the shadow storage area could not grow. Backups relying on VSS may fail.
fix: Free space or increase shadow storage (vssadmin resize shadowstorage)

entries.title: Volume Shadow Copy error
entries.what: VSS hit an unexpected error calling a routine. Backups and restore points may fail.
causes: Broken VSS writer from third-party software
fix: Run: vssadmin list writers (look for writers in a failed state)
Restart the affected service or reboot
Check the error code in the message

entries.title: VSS writer callback access denied
entries.what: VSS could not query a writer callback, usually a permissions problem. Common with some backup products.
causes: Network Service lacks COM access permissions
fix: Often harmless if backups succeed; otherwise grant Network Service COM access (dcomcnfg) per your backup vendor's guidance

entries.title: VSS device I/O error
entries.what: VSS got an error talking to a volume. Snapshots of that volume may fail.
fix: Check the volume named in the message and disk health

entries.title: VSS provider error
entries.what: A shadow copy provider returned an error.
fix: Run vssadmin list providers; update or remove faulty providers

entries.title: VSS service shutting down (idle)
entries.what: The Volume Shadow Copy service stopped because it was idle. Normal.

entries.title: VSS could not start a COM server
entries.what: The Volume Shadow Copy service could not start a COM component.
fix: Check that 'COM+ System Application' and 'Volume Shadow Copy' services are not disabled

entries.title: Check Disk result
entries.what: Result of a chkdsk scan. The message says whether problems were found and fixed.
fix: If problems were found, check disk health

entries.title: Drive optimization completed
entries.what: Windows optimized (defragmented or trimmed) a drive. Normal maintenance.

entries.title: Drive optimization could not run
entries.what: Optimization was skipped for a volume (often not supported, e.g. some USB or virtual drives). Usually harmless.
